guard: cotal_spawn exposes join, bounds it by the caller's read ACL before invoke, and carries join plus the caller's own ACL into the manager's spawn command
why: A helper spawned from a seat on #general started on no channel, with no argument on the peer
door to say otherwise, so its first cotal_send was refused and it fell back to DMs for
everything. The manager already accepted subscribe lists; the door never sent them.
J1 drops join at the manager command boundary. J2 drops the caller's ACL, so a channel-less
persona is back to the empty grant. J3 removes the read-ACL bound, so a spawn could hand on a
channel the caller may not read itself. J4 hides join from every MCP host. Each is its own
user-visible failure with its own named cell.

mutations.name: J2 drop the caller's ACL from the spawn command
mutations.find: persona: opts?.persona, callerAcl: { allowSubscribe: this.config.allowSubscribe, allowPublish: this.config.allowPublish } };
